title: A single semicolon inside a SQL block is kept verbatim
rule: SQL blocks end only at ;;, so a single ; inside the SQL is part of the SQL.

provisional.question: Every SQL block in the documentation's examples ends with ;;, but no page states that ;; is what ends a SQL block or that a single ; inside one is kept. Does Looker keep a single ; inside a SQL block?
provisional.pinned_to: lkml 1.3.7, the LookML parser DataHub, OpenMetadata and Dagster use, which ends a SQL block only at ;;

citations.quote: The sql block for dimensions can generally take any valid SQL that would go into a single column of a SELECT statement.
Declares the SQL query for a derived table.

rationale: The case's SQL is valid SQL with a semicolon inside a string literal. The citation that stated the rule, a Looker Community article, can no longer be fetched, so the case is provisional until Looker is checked.

derived_table.sql: SELECT id FROM raw.orders WHERE note != ';'
